title: 11 - Keycloak Identity
description:
**Purpose:** authentication and identity observability for the core Keycloak (`utm-core/keycloak`) — login activity, failures, realm and client inventory, and service health.

**Data sources:** `keycloak.event_entity` and the Keycloak schema via the read-only `grafana_ro` account; Prometheus for pod health.

**Privacy:** no usernames, emails or IP addresses are queried. Only opaque user UUIDs, for distinct counts.

**Known gap:** Keycloak exposes no Prometheus metrics here (`KC_METRICS_ENABLED` unset, `/metrics` → 404), so runtime panels are container-level only. See the note at the foot of the dashboard.

**Note:** this queries a live transactional database. All panels aggregate; refresh is 5m by design.

panels.title: Auth Events
panels.description: All rows in keycloak.event_entity (all time).

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.event_entity

panels.title: Auth Failures
panels.description: Events whose type ends in _ERROR. Non-zero means clients or users are failing to authenticate.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.event_entity WHERE type LIKE '%ERROR%'

panels.title: Authenticating Users
panels.description: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id). Opaque UUIDs only — no usernames or emails are read.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS value FROM keycloak.event_entity WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL

panels.title: Realms
panels.description: Configured realms.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.realm

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: OIDC clients across all realms.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.client

panels.title: Keycloak Users
panels.description: Identities in keycloak.user_entity.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.user_entity

panels.title: Authentication Events Over Time
panels.description: Hourly buckets from keycloak.event_entity, split by event type. CLIENT_LOGIN is service-to-service (client credentials); LOGIN is an interactive user sign-in.

targets.rawSql: SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(event_time/1000/3600)*3600) AS time, type AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.event_entity WHERE $__timeFilter(FROM_UNIXTIME(event_time/1000)) GROUP BY time, type ORDER BY time

panels.title: Events by Type
panels.description: Confirmed types: CLIENT_LOGIN, LOGIN, CODE_TO_TOKEN, CODE_TO_TOKEN_ERROR.

targets.rawSql: SELECT type, COUNT(*) AS events FROM keycloak.event_entity GROUP BY type ORDER BY events DESC

panels.title: Authentication by Client
panels.description: Which OIDC clients are authenticating, and how. A client that suddenly stops appearing here has lost its integration.

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.client_id AS Client, r.name AS Realm, e.type AS `Event Type`, COUNT(*) AS Events, MAX(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.event_time/1000)) AS `Last Seen` FROM keycloak.event_entity e LEFT JOIN keycloak.realm r ON r.id = e.realm_id GROUP BY e.client_id, r.name, e.type ORDER BY Events DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Interactive Logins vs Service Logins
panels.description: LOGIN (human sign-in) against CLIENT_LOGIN (service accounts). Service traffic normally dominates by orders of magnitude.

targets.rawSql: SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(event_time/1000/3600)*3600) AS time, CASE WHEN type='LOGIN' THEN 'interactive login' WHEN type='CLIENT_LOGIN' THEN 'service login' ELSE type END AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.event_entity WHERE $__timeFilter(FROM_UNIXTIME(event_time/1000)) GROUP BY time, metric ORDER BY time

panels.title: Failures Over Time
panels.description: Any event type containing _ERROR. A spike here is an authentication outage — this is the panel that would have surfaced the Grafana OAuth failure on 2026-09-21 without reading pod logs.

targets.rawSql: SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(event_time/1000/3600)*3600) AS time, CONCAT(type, ' / ', IFNULL(NULLIF(error,''),'no detail')) AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM keycloak.event_entity WHERE type LIKE '%ERROR%' AND $__timeFilter(FROM_UNIXTIME(event_time/1000)) GROUP BY time, metric ORDER BY time

panels.title: Failure Detail
panels.description: Grouped by client and error reason. `invalid_client_credentials` means a wrong or missing client secret; `invalid_grant` means bad user credentials.

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.client_id AS Client, e.type AS `Event Type`, IFNULL(NULLIF(e.error,''),'(none)') AS Error, COUNT(*) AS Count, MIN(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.event_time/1000)) AS `First Seen`, MAX(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.event_time/1000)) AS `Last Seen` FROM keycloak.event_entity e WHERE e.type LIKE '%ERROR%' GROUP BY e.client_id, e.type, Error ORDER BY Count DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Realms
panels.description: Per-realm identity and client counts, straight from the Keycloak schema.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.name AS Realm, IF(r.enabled=1,'enabled','DISABLED') AS Status, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM keycloak.user_entity u WHERE u.realm_id=r.id) AS Users, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM keycloak.client c WHERE c.realm_id=r.id) AS Clients, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM keycloak.keycloak_role k WHERE k.realm_id=r.id) AS Roles FROM keycloak.realm r ORDER BY Users DESC

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: OIDC clients by realm. `service account` clients authenticate as themselves (CLIENT_LOGIN); `public` clients are browser-facing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT c.client_id AS Client, r.name AS Realm, IF(c.enabled=1,'enabled','DISABLED') AS Status, IF(c.public_client=1,'public','confidential') AS Type, IF(c.service_accounts_enabled=1,'yes','no') AS `Service Account` FROM keycloak.client c LEFT JOIN keycloak.realm r ON r.id=c.realm_id ORDER BY r.name, c.client_id LIMIT 100

panels.title: Pod Ready
panels.description: kube_pod_status_ready for utm-core/keycloak. 0 means the identity provider is down and nothing on the platform can authenticate.

panels.title: Restarts (24h)
panels.description: Container restarts in the last day.

panels.title: Keycloak CPU
panels.description: Container CPU cores, 5m rate.

panels.title: Keycloak Memory
panels.description: Working-set memory — what the OOM killer acts on.

panels.title: Heap Used
panels.description: base_memory_usedHeap_bytes. Live JVM heap of the core Keycloak. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Heap Utilisation
panels.description: Used heap as a fraction of max heap (-Xmx). Sustained >85% precedes GC thrash and login latency. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Live Threads
panels.description: jvm_threads_live_threads. Peak since start is jvm_threads_peak_threads. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: GC Overhead
panels.description: jvm_gc_overhead_percent -- approximate share of CPU spent in GC. NOTE: despite the metric name this is a ratio in [0..1]; it is rendered here as a percentage. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: JVM Uptime
panels.description: process_uptime_seconds. A reset here is a Keycloak restart -- correlate with the Restarts panel above and with any gap in Authentication Events. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Open File Descriptors
panels.description: process_files_open_files, against a process_files_max_files ceiling of 524,288 here. Sockets to the database and to clients count against this. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Heap: used / committed / max
panels.description: base_memory_usedHeap_bytes vs committedHeap vs maxHeap. The gap between committed and max is headroom the JVM has not claimed yet. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Memory pools by region
panels.description: jvm_memory_used_bytes broken out by pool id. G1 Eden sawtooths with allocation; a rising G1 Old Gen floor that survives collection is the leak signature. Metaspace is non-heap and is not bounded by -Xmx. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: rate(jvm_gc_pause_seconds_sum[5m]) -- seconds of stop-the-world pause per second, split by cause. Causes observed on this instance: G1 Evacuation Pause, G1 Preventive Collection, Metadata GC Threshold. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Threads by state
panels.description: jvm_threads_states_threads. A climbing 'blocked' count means lock contention -- on Keycloak that is usually the database connection pool, shown in the next row. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: CPU: process vs host
panels.description: process_cpu_usage is this JVM's own share; system_cpu_usage is the whole node. Both are ratios in [0..1] reported by the JVM, which is a different source from the container CPU panel above (cAdvisor) -- expect them to differ. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Connections Active
panels.description: agroal_active_count -- connections currently checked out by request threads. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Connections Idle
panels.description: agroal_available_count -- established connections sitting idle in the pool, ready to serve without a handshake. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Threads Awaiting a Connection
panels.description: agroal_awaiting_count. THE saturation signal for Keycloak: anything sustained above 0 means login requests are queueing for the database, not for CPU. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Pool High-Water Mark
panels.description: agroal_max_used_count -- the most connections ever simultaneously in use since start. If this pins to the configured max pool size, the pool is the bottleneck. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Pool state over time
panels.description: Active vs idle vs awaiting vs high-water mark. Read them together: active climbing while idle sits at 0 and awaiting rises is pool exhaustion. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Connection acquisition latency
panels.description: agroal_blocking_time_average_milliseconds and _max -- how long a thread waited to obtain a connection. These are cumulative-since-start gauges, not windowed, so they move slowly, and the max is a watermark that never falls. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Connection acquisition rate
panels.description: rate(agroal_acquire_count_total[5m]) -- pool checkouts per second. With http_* metrics absent this is the closest available proxy for Keycloak request throughput. Not every request touches the database, so treat it as a floor, not a count. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Connection churn
panels.description: Creation, destruction and reaping rates. Healthy steady state is near 0: the pool holds warm connections. Sustained churn means connections are being closed underneath Keycloak -- a database-side wait_timeout or an idle reap in between. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Pool faults (cumulative)
panels.description: Invalid connections rejected on validation, forced flushes, and detected leaks (connections held past the leak timeout). All three are 0 at build time. Any rise here is a genuine defect, not load. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Worker Tasks Active
panels.description: worker_pool_active on the vert.x-worker-thread pool -- blocking tasks executing right now. In Keycloak these are the authentication flows. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Worker Threads Idle
panels.description: worker_pool_idle -- spare capacity in the worker pool. Reaching 0 while the queue grows is request saturation. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Worker Queue Depth
panels.description: worker_pool_queue_size -- tasks waiting for a worker thread. Sustained above 0 means logins are queueing. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Tasks Rejected
panels.description: worker_pool_rejected_total -- work the pool refused outright. Non-zero means users were turned away, and this should never be non-zero. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Worker pool state
panels.description: Active, idle and queued, per pool. vert.x-worker-thread serves requests; vert.x-internal-blocking is framework-internal and is normally flat at zero. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Task throughput and queue delay
panels.description: Completion rate from worker_pool_completed_total, and the mean time a task spent queued before a thread picked it up, as rate(queue_delay_sum)/rate(queue_delay_count). The delay series is NO DATA while no tasks run in the window -- that is idleness, not breakage. Prometheus scraping of this endpoint began 2026-09-24; earlier ranges show NO DATA.

panels.title: Scope, data protection, and what is still not instrumented

options.content:
### What this reads

Two independent sources, deliberately kept separate:

- **Identity activity** (rows 1-4) — `keycloak.event_entity` on `core-database`, the live event log of the core Keycloak (`utm-core/keycloak`, Keycloak **23.0.5**, served at `/keycloak/auth`). Verified at build time: **3,480 events**, 2026-08-26 → now, all in the `swim` realm.
- **Runtime health** (rows 5-7) — Prometheus, scraping `/keycloak/auth/metrics` since **2026-09-24**. Any range before that date is legitimately **NO DATA**, not a failure. This dashboard defaults to `now-30d`, so narrow the time picker to see the runtime rows populated.

### Data protection

`grafana_ro` holds SELECT on counting columns only. Deliberately **not** granted, so unreachable even from Explore: `IP_ADDRESS`, `DETAILS_JSON`, `DETAILS_JSON_LONG_VALUE`, `SESSION_ID`, and every username/email column on `user_entity`. `USER_ID` is an opaque UUID used only for `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` and is never displayed. The Prometheus metrics carry no personal data at all.

### Runtime metrics — what was closed, and how

An earlier version of this panel said Keycloak published no Prometheus metrics at all. **That gap is now partially closed.** `KC_METRICS_ENABLED=true` and `KC_HEALTH_ENABLED=true` were set on the deployment; the rollout surged a new pod before removing the old one (`maxSurge` 1 / `maxUnavailable` 0, no PVC), so authentication was not interrupted. The endpoint now serves **153 metric lines**.

Scraping is via a dedicated headless `keycloak-metrics` Service plus a ServiceMonitor, because the existing `keycloak` Service carries no labels for a selector to match and is a NodePort serving live authentication — not something to edit for a scrape. No existing object was modified. Target is `up`, job label `keycloak-metrics`.

**Now available, and shown above:** JVM heap and memory pools, GC pause and overhead, threads by state, process and host CPU, file descriptors, uptime; the full Agroal database connection pool; and the Vert.x worker pool.

### Remaining gap — still honestly absent

| Wanted | Metric family | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Login / registration / token-issuance counters | `keycloak_*` | **NOT INSTRUMENTED** |
| HTTP request rate, latency, status codes | `http_server_requests_*` | **NOT INSTRUMENTED** |

These are **not** switched on by `KC_METRICS_ENABLED`. They come from the separate **keycloak-metrics-spi** extension, which is not bundled in this image and would have to be added to the container build. Nothing on this dashboard fabricates them.

Two partial substitutes are drawn above and labelled as such: **Connection acquisition rate** is a floor on request throughput (not every request reaches the database), and **Task throughput** counts Vert.x worker tasks. For authentication *outcomes* — who failed and why — the `event_entity` rows above remain the better source, because they carry the error reason, which a counter never would.

### Event-log retention

Keycloak expires events per realm (`realm.events_expiration`). If that is set, this dashboard's event history is bounded by it — a flat older region means expiry, not inactivity.
